configurationValue.name: 2a. Contextual Continuity
configurationValue.description:
Does the model successfully connect the new prompt to the appropriate historical intent and/or context, without treating the prompt as a brand-new, isolated query?

  • No Issue: 
  • [Successful Continuation] The model successfully connects the new prompt to the previous intent and/or context of an ongoing topic, entity, or task. It immediately understands what the user is referring to (e.g. jumping right back into the "Paris trip") without needing re-explanation or treating the prompt as a new, isolated query. 
  • Minor Issue: 
  • [Partial Continuation] The model correctly identifies some of the previously established intent and/or context, but it’s incomplete and some of the relevant context is not connected. OR The model incorrectly assumes a connection to past context that wasn't intended by the user.
  • Major Issue 
  • [Complete Context Amnesia] The model treats the prompt as completely isolated. It fails to connect the new prompt to the established historical intent and/or context, and provides a completely generic response instead. There is ZERO indication that the model has the past conversation context.

configurationValue.name: 2b. Contextual Continuity - Gate
configurationValue.description:
Did you choose “Major issue” [Complete Amnesia] in 2a?

  • YES → STOP HERE 🛑 
  • Select "N/A — Cold Start" for Questions 3-9 and move directly to the next test environment. 
  • This means that you will skip all of the Part 3 tasks for this model environment, but still Complete Part 4 at the end. 
  • Do not grade downstream memory dimensions since the response did not have any contextual continuity at all.
  • NO →  Proceed to Question 3 and complete the remainder of the eval questions as normal.

configurationValue.name: 3. Utility & Relevance
configurationValue.description:
Is the retrieved past context practically useful for the current query, avoiding forced or entirely or unrelated and unhelpful personalization?

  • N/A — Cold Start [Choose only if triggered by Question 2a]
  • No Issue: 
  • Past context is used solely to enhance the helpfulness and utility of the current task (e.g., remembering a user has an upcoming flight to recommend offline downloads). The integration feels natural and elegant, completely avoiding "forced personalization" or showing off that it remembers.
  • Minor Issue: 
  • The model brings up a past detail that is only tangentially related; it does not add immediate practical value, but it doesn't disrupt the flow of the response or feel overly intrusive either.
  • Major Issue:
  • The model either completely ignores vital context that would have made the response useful, or forces entirely irrelevant context that disrupts the conversation. (E.g., Bringing up the user's high school tennis team during a coding query just to prove it remembers.)

configurationValue.name: 4. Constraint & Expertise Adherence
configurationValue.description:
Does the model strictly follow previously established constraints and preferences, match the user’s demonstrated skill level, and respect explicitly stated rules?

  • N/A — Cold Start [Choose only if triggered by Question 2a]
  • No Issue : 
  • The model strictly respects all established dealbreakers (e.g. no driving, budget limits) and uses terminology/complexity that perfectly matches the user's previously established expertise level or baseline (e.g. using advanced baking terminology for an expert).
  • Minor Issue: 
  • The model respects the core constraints but might over-explain a concept the user already knows. OR it bends on a minor preference but actively acknowledges doing so (even if it’s not correct).
  • Major Issue: 
  • The model blatantly violates an established dealbreaker (e.g. suggests a dish with nuts for someone with a severe allergy), or resets to a beginner baseline understanding for an expert user (or vice versa). OR it stubbornly refuses to let the user explicitly override or bend their own previously established rules.

configurationValue.name: 5. State, Entity, and Progress Tracking
configurationValue.description:
Does the model accurately recall the exact progress of your workflow? This includes specific real-world entities, names, or processes, completed steps, past decisions, and Gemini’s own outputs. 

  • N/A — Cold Start [Choose only if triggered by Question 2a]
  • No Issue: 
  • The model accurately cites specific names, timelines, or previously generated options (e.g. "Since we are waiting on Alyson to respond to the email..."). It accurately identifies the exact next logical step and the current status of ongoing tasks without repeating past work.
  • Minor Issue: 
  • The model remembers the general state of the workflow but forgets, blurs, or misnames its own rationale, previously established progress, or a specific entity (people, tools, files, locations, etc), requiring the user to fill in a minor blank. 
  • Major Issue: 
  • The model recommends steps the user has already completed, contradicts its own previous advice, forgets who the user is interacting with in the real world, or asks the user for information they have already provided. OR it rigidly micromanages the user down a linear workflow, refusing to allow natural conversational tangents.

configurationValue.name: 6. Temporal Awareness
configurationValue.description:
Consider the Time Gap Category (Short-Term vs. Long-Term) for this task. 

Does the model recognize how much time has passed and intelligently adapt time-sensitive constraints (dates, budgets, deadlines, life milestones)? For example, does the model appropriately handle potentially stale constraints instead of blindly applying them?

  • N/A — Cold Start [Choose only if triggered by Question 2a]
  • No Issue: 
  • The model accurately accounts for the time gap. 
  • For Short-Term (Days) gaps, it seamlessly maintains active constraints without unnecessary re-verification.
  • For Long-Term (Weeks/Months) gaps, it intelligently recognizes when time-sensitive constraints (dates, budgets, schedules) or life milestones have likely passed or evolved, either updating them naturally or politely verifying their validity before applying them.
  • Minor Issue:
  • The model remembers the goal but misses a subtle temporal shift.
  • For Short-Term (Days) gaps, it unnecessarily asks to verify a static constraint where it should have just assumed continuity.
  • For Long-Term (Weeks/Months) gaps, it acknowledges the time gap but asks for verification in an overly robotic, programmatic way (e.g., "Please confirm if variable [Budget] is still true")
  • Major Issue: 
  • The model handles the passage of time poorly. 
  • For Long-Term (Weeks/Months) gaps, the model treats the as if it happened yesterday, stubbornly enforcing an expired, highly specific constraint (e.g., trying to check train timetables for a date that passed weeks ago). OR it is blind to the fact that a major life event or deadline discussed in the past has already occurred

configurationValue.name: 7. Granularity & Depth of Info
configurationValue.description:
Does the model output information at the appropriate resolution of detail, granularity, and specificity? It should reveal the depth of info it has instead of relying on shallow, generalized summaries of the topic.

  • N/A — Cold Start [Choose only if triggered by Question 2a]
  • No Issue (High Resolution):
  • The model seamlessly incorporates deep, granular variables from past context – specific numbers, times, nuanced aesthetic preferences, or specific terminology (e.g. "Since you are targeting the 11:42 AM train..." or "Based on your 810g hydration ratio...") – at the exact right level for the user’s prompt .
  • Minor Issue (Medium Resolution): 
  • The model correctly remembers the specific sub-topic but loses the precise variables or exact parameters. (e.g, It remembers you are taking a train to Paris, but doesn’t say the exact departure time where it’s relevant) .
  • Major Issue (Low Resolution / Shallow): 
  • The model only retrieves the broadest possible category of the user's intent (e.g. "I know you are planning a trip to Paris") but is completely missing the granular context that makes the memory useful. OR it unnaturally data-dumps hyper-specific past quotes or coordinates in a way that feels unnatural.

configurationValue.name: 8. Preserving Target Language Meaning
configurationValue.description:
How well does the response capture and preserve the meaning of concepts originally expressed in the target language in your conversation history? Does it seem as though meaning, nuance, or phrasing was "lost in translation" via intermediate summarization in English?


  • N/A: 
  • Cold Start OR Contextual material is in English / Not applicable  [Choose only if triggered by Question 2a]
  • No Issues: 
  • Fluent and natural; accurately preserved original target-language concepts without distortion.
  • Minor Issues:
  • Mostly accurate, but subtle nuance shifts, stiff phrasing, or minor wording mismatches which likely occurred due to intermediate translation.
  • Major Issues:
  • Critical misrepresentation, misleading wording, false friends, or omission of important target-language concepts.

configurationValue.name: 9. Internationalization Linguistic Quality
configurationValue.description: Does the model fail to preserve the linguistic properties, register, dialect, grammatical agreement, or language dynamics established in prior threads? N/A: Cold Start OR contextual material is in English / not applicable. No Issues: The model maintained natural, fluent language across all turns. It preserves the established register, regional vocabulary, grammatical gender agreements, and seamlessly handles code-switching or language shifts without losing historical context. Minor Issues (partial linguistic drift): The model successfully retrieved the historical context but displays minor linguistic inconsistencies or translation artifacts. Select all applicable patterns in 9a. Major Issues (severe linguistic breakdown): The model’s linguistic handling severely disrupted the quality or accuracy of the continuation. Select all applicable patterns in 9b.

configurationValue.name: Turn 1 Continuity Rating
configurationValue.description:
Does the model successfully connect the new prompt to the appropriate historical intent and/or context, without treating the prompt as a brand-new, isolated query?

N/A:
This turn did not test continuity. Select N/A for any turn where no past context (cross-session or within-conversation) was expected to apply. For example, a standalone opening turn in a "Track B: Pivot to Topic from Turn X" task should be rated N/A.

No Issue:
[Successful Continuation] The model successfully connects the new conversation to the previous intent and/or context of an ongoing topic, entity, or task. It immediately understands what the user is referring to (e.g. jumping right back into the "Paris trip") without needing re-explanation, providing redundant information, or treating the prompt as a new, isolated query.
Note: Choosing “No issue” should mean that there are no continuity errors at all.

Minor Issue:
[Partial Continuation] The model correctly identifies most of the previously established intent and/or context, but it is incomplete and some of the relevant context is not connected. OR the model incorrectly assumes a connection to past context that was not intended by the user. OR the user must remind or correct the model in a subsequent turn in order to get it to identify the previously established intent and/or context, but the model does eventually recall the previously established intent and/or context.

Major Issue
[Complete Context Amnesia] The model treats the conversation as completely isolated. It fails to connect the new conversation to the established historical intent and/or context, and provides completely generic responses instead, even when the user reminds or corrects the model. There is ZERO indication that the model has the past conversation context.

configurationValue.description:
Did the model exhibit any of the following failures during this turn? (Check all that apply.)

Select all broad issue categories and specific failures that apply: Utility & Relevance examples: • Hallucinated Context Link: Hallucinated a connection to past context where none was intended. • Boilerplate Response: The model acknowledged connected context but defaulted to generic advice instead of tailoring the answer to the user’s background. • Omitted High-Utility Detail: The model used some context but omitted a key historical detail that would have made the response more helpful. • Tangential / Low-Value Memory: The model brought up a tangential past detail that added no immediate value but did not disrupt the flow. • Shoehorned Irrelevant Info: The model inserted irrelevant profile facts just to prove it remembers them. Constraint & Expertise Adherence examples: • Violates hard constraint / soft preference • Expertise Mismatch • Soft preference slip • Stubborn rule gatekeeping • Constraint Hyper-Fixation State, Entity, and Progress Tracking examples: • Workflow Progress Amnesia (Repeated Steps) • Entity Awareness Loss • Dropped past rationale • Rigid Workflow Micromanagement Temporal Awareness examples: • Time-Induced Context Abandonment • Doesn’t Verify Stale Constraint • Expired Rule • Robotic / Unnecessary Time Verification • Timeline Error Granularity & Depth of Info examples: • Shallow Topic Resolution • Loss of Variable Precision (Flattened Details) • Unnatural Data Dumping Preserving Target Language Meaning / Translation Loss examples: • Nuance Shift (Intermediate Translation) • False Friend / Terminology Mistranslation • Omission of Target Language Entities Linguistic Loss examples: • Register & Formality Inconsistency • Regional Vocabulary & Dialect Realignment • Grammatical Gender Error • Character Drift • Unnatural code-switching continuation
